q-cf-fit.label: Choose between the confused words
q-cf-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank, and the pair it is usually confused with among the options.

q-cf-spot.label: The confused word inside a sentence
q-cf-spot.summary: One part of the sentence uses the partner word by mistake.

rules.text: Several pairs differ only as noun and verb: advice (noun) / advise (verb), practice (noun) / practise (verb), effect (noun) / affect (verb), licence (noun) / license (verb). Decide which part of speech the slot needs first.
rules.ok: Take my advice; I advise you to wait. The effect was clear; it did not affect me.
rules.bad: Take my advise; the affect was clear.

rules.text: Some pairs differ by one letter and have nothing else in common: principal (chief, or head of a college) / principle (a rule); stationary (not moving) / stationery (paper and pens); complement (completes) / compliment (praise); desert (sand) / dessert (sweet).

Some pairs are close in sense and so get swapped: eminent (famous) / imminent (about to happen); continual (repeated with breaks) / continuous (without a break); childish (silly) / childlike (innocent); economic (of the economy) / economical (thrifty); credible (believable) / credulous (too ready to believe).
rules.ok: An eminent judge warned of an imminent crisis.
rules.bad: An imminent judge warned of an eminent crisis.

rules.text: Lie, rise and sit take no object; lay, raise and set take one. Lie-lay-lain is to rest; lay-laid-laid is to put something down.
rules.ok: He lies down after lunch. He laid the book on the table.
rules.bad: He lays down after lunch. He lied the book on the table.

q-cf-fit.cue: A blank with two look-alike or sound-alike words among the four options.
q-cf-fit.standard: Decide what part of speech and what meaning the slot needs, then pick the member of the pair that has it.
q-cf-fit.fast: For noun-and-verb pairs, test whether 'a' or 'the' could stand in front of the blank: if it could, the noun is wanted.
q-cf-fit.eliminate: Cross out the unrelated options first; the real choice is almost always between two of the four.
traps: Advice and advise, practice and practise, effect and affect.
Principal and principle, stationary and stationery.
Eminent and imminent, continual and continuous, credible and credulous.

q-cf-spot.cue: A long sentence in which one word of a confused pair has been used for the other.
q-cf-spot.standard: Read each part and test any word you know to have a twin. Replace it with its partner and see which reading makes sense.
q-cf-spot.fast: Scan for the known pairs first: lie/lay, affect/effect, principal/principle.
q-cf-spot.eliminate: Parts with no word from a confused pair can be skipped.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
After the long journey / he went upstairs / to lay down for an hour / before dinner.
options: to lay down for an hour
practice.why: 'Lay' needs an object. To rest one's own body is 'to lie down', so it should be 'to lie down for an hour'.

a.note: 'After the long journey' is a correct phrase of time.

b.note: 'He went upstairs' is a correct main clause.

d.note: 'Before dinner' is a correct phrase of time.

practice.text:

practice.why: 'Comprise' already means 'consist of', so it takes no 'of': the committee comprises nine members.

a.note: 'The chairman said' is a correct reporting clause.

c.note: 'Nine members' is the object and holds no error.

d.note: 'Three of them officials' is a correct phrase in apposition.

practice.text:

practice.why: The head of a college is the 'principal'; 'principle' is a rule or a basic truth.

b.note: 'Addressed the new students' is a correct verb with its object.

c.note: 'In the main hall' is a correct phrase of place.

d.note: 'On Monday morning' is a correct phrase of time.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The sudden change in the rules / will effect every candidate / who applied / before the first of June.
options: The sudden change in the rules
practice.why: The verb is 'affect'; 'effect' is the noun for a result. It should be 'will affect every candidate'.

a.note: 'The sudden change in the rules' is a correctly built subject.

c.note: 'Who applied' is a correct relative clause.

d.note: 'Before the first of June' is a correct phrase of time.
